subject: common tailorbird
title: This Tiny Bird Sews Its Nest With Spider Silk

scenes.text: This tiny bird doesn't build a nest. It sews one.
The common tailorbird lives across South and Southeast Asia, hiding in dense leaves.
It pokes tiny holes along the edges of a large leaf, using its sharp bill as a needle.
Then it pulls spider silk or plant fibre through, drawing the leaf into a green cradle.
The holes are so small the leaf stays green, and the fibres fluff out like rivets.
Inside that living pocket, the nest hides in plain sight. A bird with its own sewing kit.

description:
The common tailorbird sews leaves together with spider silk or plant fibre to hide its nest.
Its holes are so tiny that the leaf stays green, and the stitches work like rivets.
